items.title: Show HN: Prototype of a product management tool for AI agent companies
items.summary: Hi HN, I'm a solo founder. Teams building AI agents in a specific domain (legal, healthcare, etc.) have to piece together customer, product and market signals to decide which features to build next for their agent. This prototype is a product management tool that automates that manual process for PMs and helps them manage the agentic product. It currently runs on sample data (a fictional loans and insurance company). I'm about to start the MVP, and I'd love feedback from AI agent builders and PMs. In particular: how do you decide what to build today, and what would v1 need to do for you to try it? items.title: Show HN: Arbituro
items.summary: Looking for some honest feedback, set me straight! Over the past year I've built Arbituro, its a work management tool. Its built on the assumption that a lot of the work going forward will be done by agents, and that the hard part is no longer doing the work but agreeing when it’s finished. I've built a contract into the tool, with "done-when" clauses, and I give the agents the option of claiming work is done, but it ends up with you the owner to judge if what has been done is satisfactory. Looking forward and appreciate in advance anyone who takes the time Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50544381 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

items.title: Show HN: Neopane. Run Neovim once, show its windows in your multiplexer's panes
items.summary: Hi HN, I built a tool that allows neovim to use your native terminal multiplexer's splits instead of drawing its own. :vsplit opens a new tmux/zellij/herdr pane and it's the same neovim process behind each pane. I have not tested on linux yet, but I daily drive it on macOS (I even have nvim aliased to it!). Really looking forward to receiving feedback from all mux users to provide polish. You may ask "What's the use case?" when looking at the video, but it's less about looks and more about feel. You stop fighting your muxer and neovim and instead have them working together seamlessly. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50544553 Points: 2 # Comments: 1
